About

I came to college planning to go into medicine. A year in, engineering pulled me a different direction: I sat in on classes and talked to professors, and after hearing the SAE Formula racing team testing their car outside the engineering building, I was hooked.

I didn't expect to enjoy math, but I like working through a hard problem until the answer holds up. I'm most drawn to biomedical devices, prosthetics especially, since I still want work that helps people directly. I also love aerospace and automotive, which is why my projects range from a Braille-reading glove to vehicle aerodynamics.

Artificial Muscle Prosthetic

Research & Feasibility Study
SIMULINK
AUG – DEC 2025
Research Summary
  • Materials Considered 3D-printed carbon fiber composite for the main structure, TPU filament for flexible moving parts, aluminum for rigid bracing and hinges, and a leather-and-foam interior cuff for fit and comfort.
  • Actuation Method Pneumatic tubes that expand and contract to mimic muscle lengthening/shortening, triggered by EMG sensors reading muscle activity; hand and finger joints add kevlar wire and servo motors for finer, more stable movement.
  • Key Tradeoff Balancing structural rigidity (aluminum, carbon fiber) against flexibility and comfort (TPU, mesh, leather) while keeping the suit light enough to wear.
  • Feasibility Conclusion Landed on a viable actuation and materials approach; open questions remaining center on compressor/pneumatic sourcing, EMG sensor selection, and eventually training a movement-classification model from user testing data.
Role

Assisted in the research and feasibility phase as part of a 5-person team.

What it does

Evaluated pneumatic artificial muscle actuation for a wrist/forearm prosthetic, assessing ergonomics and joint-alignment constraints, modeling joint motion in Simulink, and proposing an EMG / IMU / pressure-sensing control architecture for future prototyping.
